newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHENS BOURSE PRES SUES 11 IN DELTA SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: ATHENS BOURSE PRES SUES 11 IN DELTA SCANDAL.

text.p: Athens stock exchange president Manolis Xanthakis, also the president of the exchange's guarantee fund, has filed suit against 11 individuals involved in the Delta Securities scandal, the bourse said in a statement.
The suit asks for the prosecution and exemplary punishment of the 11 individuals for the material and moral damages they caused to the exchange's guarantee fund.
The individuals named in the suit are the following:
D. Argyriadis, P. Tryfon, A. Dikos, T. Demosthenes, D. Koukouvetsios, E. Pitouli (wife of Tryfon), D. Harisopoulos, S. Giavridis, B. Kostopoulos, S. Yasafakis and E. Hatzakis.

The suit claims that during the October-31-to- November-6 1996 period "the Tryfon group and all others named in the suit were selling large quantities of shares in Magrizos, Mills St. George, Parnassos, Hellenic Sugar, etc. from various brokers. The same individuals were buying them back at the same time always through Delta Securities."

"...While they were receiving (cash) on their sales, or netted these amounts with buy orders of select 'good' shares, they would not make cash payments to Delta Securities on their share purchases," the bourse said in a statement.

The suit describes in detail all the share transactions through Delta Securities during the October 31 to November 6 period which never settled with the clearing house, resulting in a 2.6 billion drachma default, the bourse said.
As a result, the exchange's guarantee fund was forced to cover 1.3 billion drachmas of the 2.6 billion default. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
